Alex T.: FYI nightly perf job failed to produce nsys traces for the short-sequence KV-cache runs this morning. .qdrep produced but timeline empty, looks like capture never attached :confused:
Samir K.: ugh. did it exit too quickly? can you paste the nsys command + the CI step?
Alex T.: here's the snippet from the GH action (trimmed):
```yaml
- name: capture nsys trace
  run: |
    mkdir -p artifacts/trace
    nsys profile --output artifacts/trace/kv_short --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,osrt -- python -m perf_runner --seq-len 8 --iters 30
```
Alex T.: job logs show `nsys: profiling started` then immediately `nsys: profiling finished` with 0 kernels recorded.
Samir K.: possible: tiny run + continuous batching means kernels are fused into a single very-short-lived launch on the host side. nsys might not see GPU work if the process forks/exits before the agent finalizes. Try adding `--capture-range=none --capture-base=cpu` or extend runtime with a sleep to validate.
Maria G.: also check container privileges in CI runner. our earlier change to the runner image dropped ptrace/cgroup access which broke perf tools before. any recent infra change?
Alex T.: good call — infra updated the image last week. i'll try with the old image. in parallel, can we change the CI capture to use `nsys profile --output ... --capture-range=nvtx:start,stop` and wrap the workload with NVTX start/stop to guarantee region scope?
Samir K.: SG. sample command I test-locally that worked for microbench:
```bash
nsys profile --output out/kv_short --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx:start,stop --trace=cuda,osrt -- python -c "import nvtx, time; nvtx.range_push('bench'); ...; nvtx.range_pop(); time.sleep(0.2)"
```
Samir K.: note the explicit sleep after range end — gives nsys time to flush. For CI we can `sleep 0.1` in the wrapper.
Julia P.: re: artifacts: where do we want these stored? current path in CI goes to GH artifacts which expire in 7 days. perf diffs need longer retention for bisecting.
Maria G.: recommendation: upload raw trace qdrep to s3://redwood-perf/nightly/kv/$(date)/ and keep 90 days. then have the diff dashboard point at the latest two prefixes.
ci-bot: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/nightly/kv/2026-03-17/1893456789-kv_short.qdrep -> https://s3.redwood.example/.. :white_check_mark:
Alex T.: thanks. after running with the old runner image + NVTX/short-sleep we got a proper timeline and several kernel launches. main hotspot: cuBLAS matmul at 2ms but there's a weird extra memcpy kernel preceding it on the short sequences. looks like the kernel selector is choosing a layout-conversion kernel pre-call.
Samir K.: that maps to the kernel-picker change last week (fallthrough: prefer layout-conversion when batch_size==1). i think for short sequences the runtime should skip layout conversion (cost > benefit).
Alex T.: profiling snippet (nvprof-like timeline):
```
00:00.000 memcpy_h2d (copy) 0.15ms
00:00.150 layout_convert_kernel 0.9ms
00:01.050 cublas_gemm 2.1ms
00:03.150 memcpy_d2h 0.2ms
```
Alex T.: that convert kernel is ~30–40% of the critical path on seq=8. For throughput runs (seq=1024) it's negligible.
Samir K.: two follow-ups: (1) add a heuristic in the picker: if seq_len < 64 and batch_size <=2, disable layout-conversion; (2) add an opt-in CI microbenchmark that runs seq in {8,32,128} and auto-attaches NVTX so diffs show regression.
Julia P.: on the diff dashboard side: we should surface percent-change in p50/p95 end-to-end and list top-3 kernel deltas (by delta time). Also mark changes that are only present for tiny sequences as a special tag.
Alex T.: yes — current diff UI hashes total timeline only so small-seq regressions get lost. i can add an export of per-kernel breakdown JSON (kernel_name -> time_ms) alongside qdrep.
Maria G.: retention + privacy note: raw qdrep has filepaths and envs; make sure we sanitize in the upload step before broad access. we can keep raw in private bucket and upload sanitized metrics to dashboard.
Samir K.: also want to automate capture of perfetto/CPU traces for the host-side hotpaths (scheduling stalls). perfetto + nsys together helped once when we tracked a 70ms wait in the scheduler. perf-bot: can we add a perfetto post-step?
perf-bot: suggested job template updated: `perfetto record --output artifacts/trace/host.pb --duration 30` and `nsys profile ...` in parallel, then bundle. tagging is `nvtx` + `perftrace` for correlation.
Alex T.: plan of action:
- change CI runner back to previous image for nightly perf (temp) ✅
- update nsys invocation to use NVTX start/stop + short sleep ✅
- implement picker heuristic PR to skip layout-conversion for tiny sequences (samir) -> WIP
- add microbench workflow that writes qdrep + per-kernel JSON -> next week
- upload raw qdrep to private s3 w/ 90d retention and publish sanitized metrics to dashboard (maria)

Samir K.: i'll draft the picker change and add unit tests with kernel cost estimates. Alex, can you attach the qdrep that shows the memcpy->convert->gemm path? drop to s3 path or GH artifact.
Alex T.: uploaded to s3 and linked earlier. i'll also paste a tiny screenshot of the timeline in the PR.
Julia P.: ok looks good. once we have microbench outputs, i'll wire the diff dashboard to parse per-kernel JSON and flag >10% regressions. :rocket:
Maria G.: also adding a short-run smoke check in pre-merge to catch obvious capture regressions (fail job if qdrep missing).
Alex T.: awesome — thanks everyone. i'll follow up with the PRs and CI tweaks.
per-bot: reaction :thumbsup: (not a real user, just confirming)
